prompt: Refactor safe_join and Windows path normalization

memory.claim: On Windows, safe_join currently accepts special device filenames such as CON and NUL. It should return None for Windows special device names, while preserving ordinary joins and traversal rejection. Do not open any Windows device; this is string validation only. Tests execute on Linux: emulate the Windows branch by replacing the target module-local os reference (werkzeug.security.os) with a SimpleNamespace(name="nt", path=posixpath), without changing the global os module. Without Windows emulation, CON remains an ordinary Linux filename and must still be accepted.

audit.explanation: The proposed revision violated at least one recalled behavioral memory.

analysis.summary: safe_join does not filter out Windows reserved device names when the Windows branch is emulated, allowing paths like 'trusted/CON' to be returned instead of None.
analysis.likely_cause: The function lacks a Windows-specific validation step that rejects reserved filenames (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1‑9, LPT1‑9) when os.name == 'nt'.
analysis.next_experiment: Add a conditional block in safe_join that, when os.name == 'nt', checks the final path component against a set of Windows reserved names (case‑insensitive) and returns None if matched; verify with the existing emulated test.

limitations: Only selected historical behaviors were replayed; this is not universal correctness.
A preserved memory means its frozen regression passed in the recorded audit environment.
Refactoring may make an old test uncertain until its behavioral claim is reviewed and adapted.
